item.title: T20 World Cup 2026: WATCH- ‘Unka taqat nahi hai, style nahi hai chakka marna’- Mohd. Kaif's cheeky dig at Babar Azam on-air

item.title: Afghanistan’s Rahmanullah Gurbaz withdraws from PSL 2026; Taliban government refuses NOC to play in Pakistan- Report
item.description: Afghanistan’s Taliban government has reportedly refused to grant NOCs to their players to participate in the upcoming Pakistan Super League (PSL 2026), resulting in Rahmanullah Gurbaz pulling out of the competition. Gurbaz was signed directly by Peshawar Zalmi for an undisclosed sum just a day before. item.title: T20 World Cup 2026: Indian cricket fraternity reacts as India defeats USA by 29 runs, Mohammed Siraj takes 3 wickets
item.description: India opened their T20 World Cup 2026 tournament against the USA on February 7, 2026. The Group A match was played at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. item.title: “My plan was to see Real Madrid game on 15th”: Mohammed Siraj opens on his late T20 World Cup 2026 call-up
item.description: Mohammed Siraj played a key role with the ball in India’s 29-run victory over the USA on the opening day of the T20 World Cup 2026 at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai. The right-arm quick, who joined the squad on Friday (February 6) after Harshit Rana was ruled out of the tournament due to a knee injury, returned with figures of 3/29 in four overs. item.description: Paul van Meekeren rued the missed opportunity to end Pakistan's ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026 campaign on the opening day of the tournament itself, asserting that the Netherlands were the superior team in the curtain raiser played at the Sinhalese Sports Club (SSC) Ground in Colombo. item.title: “I did not sleep whole night,” U19 World Cup hero Vaibhav Sooryavanshi admits he was under pressure ahead of final
item.description: India’s teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi took the cricketing world by storm as he smashed a blistering 175 off 80 balls in the ICC U19 World Cup 2026 final in Harare on Friday (February 6). Sooryavanshi’s knock, studded with 15 fours and 15 sixes, propelled India to a gigantic total of 411/9.
